---
description: "Base R text annotations: text() and mtext() with pos, offset, padj, outer and at, for labelling individual points and adding text to the margins."
---

# Text Annotations {#textann}

## Introduction

In this chapter, we will learn to add text annotations. There are occasions when you want to display additional information in a plot. We usually do this by adding text either inside the plot or on the margins. For example, you might want to label a line or a bar, or add a formula to communicate better what is shown. The idea is to use the available space within or outside the plot to provide information that can be useful to the reader. We will add text inside as well as on the margins, using the following two functions:

- `text()` : add text inside the plot
- `mtext()` : add text on the margins of the plot

## Syntax

Let us take a quick look at the syntax of both functions:

```{r text-syntax, eval=FALSE}
text(x, y = NULL, labels = seq_along(x$x), adj = NULL,
     pos = NULL, offset = 0.5, vfont = NULL,
     cex = 1, col = NULL, font = NULL, ...)

mtext(text, side = 3, line = 0, outer = FALSE, at = NA,
      adj = NA, padj = NA, cex = NA, col = NA, font = NA, ...)
```

## Text Inside the Plot

To add text inside a plot, supply the following arguments to the `text()` function:

- `labels` : the text to be displayed
- `x` : x axis coordinate
- `y` : y axis coordinate

Below is a simple example:

```{r text1, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text')
```

The text appears at the coordinates (340, 30). Ensure that the text is enclosed in single or double quotes, and that the coordinates are within the range of the **X** and **Y** axis variables.

## Color

We can modify the color of the text using the `col` argument in the `text()` function.

```{r text2, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red')
```

The plot below shows the appearance of the text for different values of the `col` argument:

```{r text3, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
values <- c('red', 'blue', 'green')
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = i)
  mtext(paste("col = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Font

We can modify the font of the text using the `font` argument in the `text()` function.

```{r text4, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red', font = 2)
```

The plot below shows the appearance of the text for different values of the `font` argument:

```{r text5, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
values <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red', font = i)
  mtext(paste("font = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Font Family

We can modify the font family of the text using the `family` argument in the `text()` function.

```{r text6, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red', family = 'mono')
```

The plot below shows the appearance of the text for different values of the `family` argument:

```{r text7, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
values <- c('mono', 'serif', 'sans')
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red', cex = 1.5, family = i)
  mtext(paste("family = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Font Size

We can modify the font size of the text using the `cex` argument in the `text()` function.

```{r text8, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red', cex = 2)
```

The plot below shows the appearance of the text for different values of the `cex` argument:

```{r text9, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
values <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', col = 'red', cex = i)
  mtext(paste("cex = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Text on the Margins

The `mtext()` function places text on the margins of the plot. It allows us to modify the location of the text in several ways, and we will explore them one by one. To begin with, let us add text to the plot using `mtext()`. The minimum input is the text itself:

```{r mtext1, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text')
```

As you can see, the text is placed on the margin of the plot, not inside it. Next, we will specify the margin on which to place the text.

## Specify Margin

Use the `side` argument to specify the margin on which to place the text. It takes values 1 to 4, each representing one side of the plot.

```{r mtext2, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text', side = 1)
```

The plot below displays the appearance of the text when different options for the `side` argument are supplied:

```{r mtext3, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
values <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  mtext('Sample Text', side = i)
  mtext(paste("side = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue", adj = 1)
}
par(init)
```

## Line

The `line` argument places the text at a specified distance from the margin. The default value is `0`. As the value increases, the text moves farther from the margin and outside the plot; as it decreases, the text moves inside the plot and farther from the margin. In the example below, the text is placed outside the plot because the value is greater than 1.

```{r mtext4, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text', line = 1)
```

When the value is less than `0`, the line argument places the text inside the plot.

```{r mtext5, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text', line = -1)
```

The plot below displays the appearance of the text when different values are supplied to the `line` argument:

```{r mtext6, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
values <- c(-0.5, -1, -1.5, 0.5, 1, 1.5)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  mtext('Sample Text', line = i)
  mtext(paste("line = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue", adj = 1)
}
par(init)
```

## Alignment

The `adj` argument controls the horizontal alignment of the text. It takes values between 0 and 1. If set to `0`, the text is left aligned; at `1`, it is right aligned. In the example below, the text is left aligned as `adj` is set to `0`.

```{r mtext7, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text', adj = 0)
```

When the value is set to `1`, the text is right aligned.

```{r mtext8, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text', adj = 1)
```

The plot below displays the appearance of the text when different values are supplied to the `adj` argument:

```{r mtext9, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
values <- c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  mtext('Sample Text', adj = i)
  mtext(paste("adj = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue", line = -2)
}
par(init)
```

## Position

The `pos` argument of the `text()` function places the text relative to the specified coordinates without needing `adj`. It takes values 1 to 4, each representing a position around the point:

- `1`: below
- `2`: to the left
- `3`: above
- `4`: to the right

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
#| label: fig-text-pos
#| fig-cap: "The pos argument placing text relative to a point"
#| fig-alt: "A grid of scatterplots of displacement against miles per gallon. In each panel the same single labelled point is annotated, but the label is placed in a different compass position relative to it, stepping through south-west, west, north-west, north and further around."
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
values <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', pos = i)
  mtext(paste("pos = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Offset

The `offset` argument of the `text()` function controls how far the text is placed from the coordinates when `pos` is used. The distance is measured in character widths, and the default is `0.5`.

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
#| label: fig-text-offset
#| fig-cap: "The offset argument pushing a label away from its point"
#| fig-alt: "A scatterplot of displacement against miles per gallon with one point labelled, where the label is displaced a fixed distance from the point rather than sitting on top of it."
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
text(x = 340, y = 30, labels = 'Sample Text', pos = 3, offset = 1.5)
```

## Perpendicular Adjustment

The `padj` argument of the `mtext()` function fine-tunes the placement of the text in the direction perpendicular to `adj`. It takes values between 0 and 1. Compare the two plots below and observe the nudge:

```{r mtextpadj, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
values <- c(0, 1)
for (i in values) {
  plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
  mtext('Sample Text', side = 3, padj = i)
  mtext(paste("padj = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue", line = -2)
}
par(init)
```

## Outer Margin

By default, `mtext()` places text on the inner margin of the current plot. Set `outer = TRUE` to place the text on the outer margin of the whole figure region instead. This is useful with multi-panel layouts, but first reserve outer space with `par(oma = ...)`:

```{r mtextouter, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(oma = c(0, 0, 3, 0))
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Outer Margin Text', outer = TRUE)
par(init)
```

## Exact Position

The `at` argument of the `mtext()` function places the text at an exact position along the margin, expressed in the user coordinates of the corresponding axis. Below, the text is anchored at `disp = 200` on the bottom margin instead of the default center:

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
#| label: fig-mtext-at
#| fig-cap: "The at argument placing margin text at specific coordinates"
#| fig-alt: "A scatterplot of displacement against miles per gallon with text added to the margin at explicitly chosen positions along the axes, rather than at the default margin locations."
plot(mtcars$disp, mtcars$mpg)
mtext('Sample Text', side = 1, at = 200)
```
